A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Render-of-Thought. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including the image-based case studies. The original case-study appendix moves from D to H.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training and decoding ablations, inference timings, and latent-representation case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds training-time measurements, evaluations using a shared backbone, and GPQA/ProsQA results in Tables 7-9.

M1.justification: The rendering procedure, visual projection head, two-stage training, losses, and dynamic/fixed-budget decoding procedures remain unchanged. Applying existing baselines to another backbone does not establish a change to RoT.

E1.justification: v3 retains GSM8k-Aug, GSM-Hard, SVAMP, MultiArith, and MATH, and adds actual evaluations on GPQA and ProsQA in Appendix F. These extend the evaluated coverage from mathematical problems to scientific question answering and logical reasoning.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain intact. New Tables 8-9 reuse Coconut, CODI, and CoLaR-2, already evaluated in v1. The documented differences concern backbone settings and task coverage; no comparator-algorithm revision is specified.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a controlled comparison placing RoT and three baselines on Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, addressing the differing backbones in retained Table 2. Appendix D introduces training-time measurements with matched three-epoch budgets, batch size 16, and one H20 GPU. Existing experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices D-E add analyses of training overhead and whether backbone differences explain RoT's advantage, substantially extending the efficiency and attribution evidence. Existing stage, projection-head, rendering, decoding, and case analyses remain unchanged. Appendix G adds discussion, not another termination experiment.

E5.justification: The five-seed/95% confidence-interval statement and existing uncertainty entries remain unchanged. New appendix tables report point values, as earlier appendix ablation tables already did; no changed run counts or statistical estimation procedures are specified.

E6.justification: Tables 7-9 add training times of 56.1 hours for RoT versus 36.9 for SFT-CoT, VLM-based comparator results including CoLaR-2's 45.3 average versus RoT's retained 55.4, and RoT Pass@1 scores of 60.5 on GPQA and 100.0 on ProsQA. Original Tables 1-6 and plotted findings are unchanged. The new backbone results are additional evaluations, not corrections or same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The loss equations, termination definition, and special-token normalization remain unchanged. Appendix G's continuous-space explanation introduces no formal assumption, theorem, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace claims of maintaining competitive performance with an efficiency-accuracy Pareto framing, qualifying the performance claim around a tradeoff. The novelty, analyzability, plug-and-play, and compression contributions remain unchanged; logical-reasoning coverage was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets the shared-backbone results as evidence against a pretraining-only explanation and argues that inference savings offset training overhead. Appendix G strengthens the termination explanation into an asserted intrinsic continuous-space difficulty, without a new causal test. Existing limitations and case interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds homepage and model-collection access links and documents hardware, epoch allocation, and measured costs for the training-time comparison. Original implementation hyperparameters remain unchanged. The new GPQA/ProsQA evaluation receives only a general statement that implementation details are consistent with the existing setup.

R1.justification: v3 adds the GPQA reference by Rein et al. and expands discussion connecting termination difficulties to the already cited LVR work. The related-work section and central novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include limited abstract/introduction wording, author-order and affiliation edits, and four new appendix sections with an expanded contents list. The case study becomes Appendix H, with updated cross-references. The existing narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds three compact appendix tables and a title-page resource strip. Figure 2 moves earlier, some tables become more compact, and appendix material shifts. Original figure content and existing table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: Table 8 addresses an important confound in v1's central baseline comparison by using the same backbone. Table 7 makes training overhead measurable, while Table 9 supplies evidence for previously claimed non-mathematical applicability. Together these substantially strengthen empirical support and transparency. Sparse task-specific documentation and absent displayed uncertainty in the new comparisons limit their strength, but do not outweigh these gains.
